active_paradigms.idea: Jointly optimize replication counts and hierarchical placements with scipy.optimize.milp
active_paradigms.description: The current program is a three-stage greedy heuristic: LPT packs raw expert-group load to nodes, greedy marginal replication is performed only inside the resulting node, and a second LPT packs replica streams to GPUs. Its strength is that every stage is vectorized across layers and always preserves the required fixed number of expert slots, ranks, and node-local replication constraint. Its key weakness is irreversible early decisions: a hot group assigned to a node can consume that node's entire replica budget, while a slightly worse node partition could permit much better final GPU maxima. Replace the whole per-layer heuristic with one scipy.optimize.milp model for small and medium evaluator cases, with binary variables representing an allowed replica-count configuration for each logical expert and binary placement variables for each resulting replica on physical GPU slots. Add exact constraints for one selected configuration per expert, all physical slots filled, each expert receiving at least one copy, GPU capacity, and node-local eligibility induced by group placement. Introduce a makespan variable T and constrain each GPU's sum of expert load divided by that expert's selected replica count to be at most T; use a tiny secondary objective for node imbalance or movement only after T. This directly attacks the likely load-balance metric rather than separately optimizing raw node load and replica-stream load, and can fall back to the present greedy result if the MILP time limit is reached.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Primary load-balance score, especially worst-GPU load after replication; secondarily retain a strict per-layer solve time budget so exact optimization is used only where it can beat greedy.
active_paradigms.cautions: The adapter shown exposes only combined_score, not the original evaluator's load formula, so first inspect the original evaluator before choosing whether T should model max load, variance, communication, or a weighted combination. MILP size grows rapidly with experts, replica-count choices, and GPUs; restrict each expert to sensible counts such as 1 through min(available slots, ceil(weight/target)) and set scipy's time_limit. Preserve the output contract exactly: every physical slot must be assigned, phyrank must be contiguous from zero for each logical expert, and log2phy scatter indices must remain valid. Do not model replicas as carrying full expert weight; each selected copy must contribute weight/count.

active_paradigms.idea: Use a single expanded convex-cost circulation via networkx.min_cost_flow
active_paradigms.description: Formulate the placement decision as a min-cost-flow graph rather than using LPT at the group and GPU stages. The current LPT policy minimizes the next local load but has no look-ahead for the fact that a GPU has a fixed number of expert slots and that node assignment determines where all future replicas may go. Build one graph per layer whose source sends one unit for every required physical expert occurrence, whose intermediate paths encode eligible logical-expert replica levels and allowed node/GPU destinations, and whose sink-side parallel arcs represent successive GPU-load bands with increasing marginal cost. Replica level k carries the effective stream load weight[e]/k, while prefix-enforcing arcs ensure that a level k replica cannot exist unless all lower replica levels of that expert exist. Encode group/node locality by simply omitting forbidden expert-to-node arcs, and encode equal slot counts by giving every GPU its exact physical-slot capacity. Calling networkx.min_cost_flow then optimizes a globally coupled convex overload surrogate in one integral flow solve, unlike the current independent greedy stages. Decode selected expert-level-to-GPU paths into phy2log and derive rank by ordering the selected levels for each expert.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: GPU tail overload and node-level congestion simultaneously, with a convex marginal cost chosen to strongly penalize the load region above the target average.
active_paradigms.cautions: This is appropriate only if evaluator dimensions are modest; NetworkX is Python-heavy and can lose badly on runtime for large dense layer instances. Loads may be floating point, whereas min-cost flow costs must be integer-like; scale and round deterministically, retaining enough precision that close expert loads do not collapse into ties. The expanded load-band construction is an approximation unless weights share an exact integer quantum, so validate the decoded placement against the evaluator rather than assuming the flow surrogate is identical to score. This must be a replacement global formulation, not a flow post-processing step after the existing LPT, because the value comes from allowing node, replica, and GPU decisions to trade off together.

active_paradigms.idea: Script the existing batched greedy policy with torch.jit.script and specialize fixed topology constants
active_paradigms.description: The present implementation is already quality-preserving relative to the original policy, but it still executes Python loops once per group and once per redundant slot in balanced_packing and replicate_experts. Its vectorization across layers is a major strength, while repeated Python dispatch, masked_fill allocation, gather/scatter launches, and scalar loop control are its primary runtime limitation. Replace the helper functions by TorchScript-compatible functions and compile the complete topology-specialized rebalance kernel once with torch.jit.script, keeping num_groups, num_nodes, num_gpus, group_size, and per-GPU capacity as specialized constants where evaluator topology is fixed. TorchScript can retain the exact LPT tie order and exact greedy replica selection while moving loop control and temporary lifetime management out of the Python interpreter. Precompute immutable arange/index templates outside the timed path and pass or cache them by shape/device, rather than reconstructing them for every rebalance invocation. This does not change the discrete assignment, so it is the lowest-risk route to improving any runtime component of combined_score while preserving the current 0.129100 balancing behavior. If evaluator score is purely load quality rather than time-sensitive, use this only as infrastructure for a guarded quality solver, not as the principal expected score improvement.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Algorithm execution time and score consistency while maintaining exactly the current valid mappings and load-balance quality.
active_paradigms.cautions: torch.compile already failed and should not be retried; TorchScript is a distinct execution path, but benchmark compile/warm-up cost must be excluded or amortized through caching. Verify bit-for-bit tie behavior because argmin/argmax ties and floating-point sort order can alter placements even when aggregate balance is similar. Avoid scripting dynamic nested Python closures and unsupported typing patterns; define top-level scripted helpers and fixed tensor dtypes. The supplied adapter forces one CPU thread, so measure in the same fresh-process setting rather than relying on GPU or multithreaded speedups.

tried_paradigms.idea: Compile and fuse the batched greedy kernels so quality-preserving balancing costs substantially less
tried_paradigms.description: The evaluator wrapper explicitly forces a fresh serial, single-threaded process and imposes a finite timeout, so algorithm execution cost can affect the combined scalar even if mapping quality is unchanged. The current implementation avoids scalar conversions but still executes Python loops over every group and every redundant replica, each containing multiple tensor dispatches such as masked fill, argmin, gather, and scatter. Wrap the core packing and replica-allocation kernels in `torch.compile` with a fixed-shape-friendly mode, keeping all tensors on CPU and compiling only after input normalization. This permits TorchInductor to fuse repeated pointwise operations, reuse buffers, and reduce Python dispatch overhead while leaving the exact LPT decisions and output maps unchanged. Use a shape-specialized cache keyed by `(layers, logical_experts, replicas, groups, nodes, gpus)` so repeated evaluator workloads do not trigger recompilation. This is a different objective axis from assignment quality: it protects the existing 0.129100-quality behavior while creating time budget for a bounded exact/exchange packing variant on difficult shapes. If compilation startup dominates a one-shot evaluation, compile only when the estimated loop work exceeds a threshold and otherwise call the eager vectorized implementation.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Runtime and timeout robustness of the current high-quality vectorized LPT/water-filling algorithm, while preserving exactly the same maps and hence avoiding balance regressions.
tried_paradigms.cautions: Compilation can have substantial first-call latency in a fresh evaluator process, so benchmark end-to-end startup rather than kernel time alone. Guard this path with `hasattr(torch, 'compile')` and retain eager behavior if compilation fails or the installed PyTorch backend lacks Inductor support. Avoid data-dependent Python branching inside compiled kernels, and verify bitwise or tie-equivalent outputs because tiny floating-point changes in `argmin` ties can alter placement and evaluator load metrics.

tried_paradigms.idea: Replica-aware group-to-node packing using a water-filling surrogate
tried_paradigms.description: The current code packs groups to nodes using raw group token sums, then decides replicas separately inside each node. This misses the key interaction: a node receiving a concentrated hot expert can dissipate that load through its available replica slots, whereas a node receiving several moderately hot experts may remain harder to balance. Before the existing node packing, compute a replica-aware effective group cost by estimating the best attainable maximum per-replica stream for each candidate node allocation, using integer water-filling on the experts in that group. Use this effective cost, rather than raw group sum, as the weight passed to the existing capacity-constrained LPT packing. The calculation can be implemented tensor-wise by sorting expert loads and evaluating the finite set of thresholds induced by load divided by replica count; no MILP, flow, or assignment solver is needed. Retain the existing hierarchy and output construction, so all placement invariants and rank semantics remain unchanged. This directly improves the first hierarchical decision, which otherwise irreversibly constrains every later replica and GPU decision. It is especially valuable when expert load is highly skewed and replicas are plentiful relative to the number of nodes.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Reduce worst node pressure and downstream GPU imbalance by making node group assignment reflect replica capacity; preserve the current vectorized runtime profile.
tried_paradigms.cautions: The surrogate must respect the exact fixed number of physical slots per node, including the mandatory first copy of every expert. Do not change group membership unless evaluator constraints explicitly permit it. Use float32 only for ordering/estimation and preserve integer maps. Since the underlying evaluator is not shown in the supplied wrapper, validate both balance score and execution time on every workload rather than assuming a raw-load surrogate is always beneficial.

tried_paradigms.idea: Bounded largest-smallest exchange refinement after LPT GPU packing
tried_paradigms.description: The final GPU placement is cardinality-constrained LPT: each replica stream is placed once, in descending order, onto the least-loaded non-full GPU. LPT is fast but can leave a large stream paired with medium streams while another GPU contains several streams whose aggregate is only slightly smaller. Add a strictly bounded local improvement pass that considers only the heaviest loaded GPU and lightest loaded GPU in each layer, selects a small fixed candidate set of their largest and smallest streams, and accepts the best feasible one-for-one swap only if it decreases the layer maximum GPU load. Evaluate swap deltas analytically from the current GPU sums, so candidate scoring is a small batched tensor operation rather than rebuilding an assignment or calling a solver. Repeat for at most a fixed 2–4 rounds, or until no improving swap exists. Because every GPU keeps exactly `phy_experts_per_gpu` streams, this refinement preserves all output shape and placement constraints. Unlike the failed min-cost-flow and Hungarian approaches, this optimizes the actual nonlinear bottleneck produced by a complete placement and uses LPT as a strong warm start rather than replacing it with a linear proxy.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Lower the per-layer peak physical-GPU replica load, which is the likely load-balance bottleneck, with predictable bounded overhead.
tried_paradigms.cautions: Never swap replica identities in a way that loses `phyrank`; carry stream indices and gather both `phy2mlog` and `phyrank` from the refined permutation. Use strict improvement with a small epsilon to avoid oscillation and deterministic tie breaking for reproducibility. Limit candidate and iteration counts aggressively because the evaluator has a runtime component and runs single-threaded. Do not use full all-pairs GPU/stream search, which can erase the vectorization advantage of the current implementation.

tried_paradigms.idea: Exact discrete threshold water-filling for replica-count allocation
tried_paradigms.description: The present replica allocator repeatedly gives the next slot to the expert with largest current `weight/count`. That greedy rule is good for minimizing the largest isolated replica stream, but it does not explicitly solve the fixed-budget minimax count allocation and can be sensitive to ties and subsequent GPU cardinality packing. Replace the sequential extra-slot loop with a threshold formulation: for a candidate stream-load threshold T, expert e requires `ceil(weight[e]/T)` copies, clipped to the available maximum; the smallest feasible T is found among the discrete breakpoints `weight[e]/k`. Select the minimum threshold whose required-copy sum fits the physical-expert budget, then distribute any leftover slots to the experts with greatest reduction from one additional copy. This gives a globally consistent minimax replica-count vector for each node/layer before GPU packing, while avoiding a Python loop over every redundant slot. Generate breakpoint ordering and leftover priorities in batched tensors, then construct `phy2log` and ranks from counts by masked sorting. This is fundamentally different from the failed MILP attempts: it exploits the separable reciprocal load structure exactly rather than expressing a weak linearized proxy. It can also be faster than the current method when there are many redundant physical slots.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Improve replica-count quality for the maximum per-copy load objective and reduce allocation cost when replica surplus is large.
tried_paradigms.cautions: Counts must remain at least one for every logical expert and sum exactly to physical slots within each node; zero-weight experts need deterministic handling because their threshold breakpoint is zero. The threshold objective alone does not account for final GPU packing, so compare it against current greedy allocation and keep the better result using an inexpensive predicted post-packing maximum if benchmark distributions are heterogeneous. Ensure the constructed replica ranks are contiguous from zero through count minus one, otherwise `log2phy.scatter_` validation/output semantics will break.

tried_paradigms.idea: Replica-aware node-group ordering using marginal overload relief (`torch.topk`)
tried_paradigms.description: The current program first assigns groups to nodes using raw group-token sums, then independently creates replicas inside each resulting node. This is fast and valid, but it treats a group containing one extremely hot expert the same as a group with the same total load spread uniformly across experts, even though the former can be reduced substantially by replicas. Compute for every group a replica-aware pressure score: simulate its unavoidable maximum replica-stream load under the local physical-slot budget, or approximate it from the top-k expert weights obtained with `torch.topk`. Use that pressure rather than only `sum(group)` as the descending order and load contribution in the existing node packing step. Keep the existing replication and GPU-packing phases unchanged, so map shapes, rank semantics, and hierarchical placement constraints remain exactly valid. This is a constructive objective correction rather than a MILP, flow, Hungarian assignment, or final-stage exchange search. It should improve cases where raw-balanced nodes have very different post-replication bottlenecks, while retaining the current batched tensor implementation and low runtime.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Primary load-balance score by balancing the post-replication bottleneck across nodes rather than balancing only pre-replication group totals; runtime should remain close to the current method because only a small top-k reduction is added.
tried_paradigms.cautions: Do not allocate replicas globally across nodes: every expert must remain represented within the node selected for its group, and all physical experts per node/GPU must still be exact. The pressure estimate must use the actual local slot count, including the mandatory one copy of every local logical expert. Preserve deterministic tie-breaking, preferably by stable ordering on original group index, because noisy ties can worsen evaluator consistency. Since the provided adapter does not expose the original evaluator’s internal metric, validate whether it measures per-GPU peak, variance, communication locality, or a combined runtime-quality score before choosing the exact pressure formula.

tried_paradigms.idea: Bounded-water-filling replica counts via prefix thresholds (`torch.searchsorted`)
tried_paradigms.description: The present `replicate_experts` greedily gives each extra slot to the expert with current largest `weight/count`, one slot at a time. That greedy rule is reasonable, but its repeated argmax sequence is a discrete approximation to minimizing the largest replica-stream load and can make inferior tie decisions when several experts cross the same threshold. For each layer-node, view a candidate stream-load cap T as requiring `ceil(weight_i/T)` copies of expert i, clipped below by one; the smallest feasible T is where the required-copy sum fits the local physical-expert count. Build the finite set of breakpoints `weight_i/k` for valid k, sort it once, and use `torch.searchsorted` to find the threshold at which the copy budget is met. Assign the resulting counts, then distribute any leftover slots by the largest exact marginal reduction from adding one copy. Emit `phy2mlog` and `phyrank` by expanding those counts in deterministic expert-index order, leaving the current GPU placement and inverse-map construction intact. This directly targets the bottleneck induced by replication rather than repeatedly selecting a current maximum stream, and it avoids the failed MILP/flow/assignment formulations entirely.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Reduce the maximum per-replica load before GPU packing, which is the dominant lower bound on any per-GPU balance objective; it can also reduce Python-loop work when redundant-slot counts are large.
tried_paradigms.cautions: The expansion must provide ranks exactly 0 through `count-1` for each logical expert, since `log2phy.scatter_` relies on that invariant. Use float32/float64 comparisons consistently and explicitly handle zero weights, where threshold division and tie behavior otherwise produce infinities or arbitrary extra replicas. Breakpoint materialization can be expensive if the number of extra slots is huge; cap candidate k values at the local physical budget and fall back to the existing greedy loop when that product is too large. This changes replica counts and therefore can trade a lower peak for a slightly different downstream LPT distribution, so compare against the existing greedy result on the evaluator workload and retain the better deterministic construction if a cheap analytical proxy is unavailable.

tried_paradigms.idea: Complementary heavy/light group pairing before hierarchical packing (`torch.argsort`)
tried_paradigms.description: The current group-to-node phase is capacity-constrained LPT on indivisible pre-existing groups, which is good for generic scheduling but can leave concentrated heavy groups together with moderately heavy groups because it only reacts to current aggregate node load. Sort groups by a lexicographic signature consisting of total weight, maximum expert weight, and predicted post-replication pressure using `torch.argsort`. Construct the node input order by pairing the heaviest remaining group with the lightest compatible group, then distribute these pairs cyclically over nodes; when more than two groups belong to a node, continue by assigning the next group to the lowest predicted-pressure partial node. The key distinction is that this is a deterministic complementary partitioning construction at the group level, not a replacement of final GPU LPT by min-cost flow, Hungarian matching, or swap descent. It deliberately counteracts correlations between group total load and group hot-expert concentration, which raw LPT does not model. Once the groups are ordered/paired, continue using the existing hierarchical replication, GPU packing, and map reconstruction code, preserving all evaluator-facing output contracts. This can be especially valuable when `groups_per_node` is small, where one unlucky indivisible group pairing dominates the node bottleneck.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Node-level imbalance and locality-constrained peak load, while retaining the current inexpensive tensor-only downstream algorithm and avoiding additional global optimization calls.
tried_paradigms.cautions: Only reorder whole groups; never split a logical group across nodes, because the hierarchy assumes contiguous group-size blocks when deriving `mlog2log`. If `groups_per_node` is one, this construction has no freedom and must exactly fall back to the current behavior. Use stable deterministic sorting and retain original indices for ties, otherwise mappings may vary between platforms. Pairing is not universally superior to LPT on purely total-load objectives, so use a deterministic lower-bound comparison of predicted maximum node pressure and choose pairing only when it beats the original LPT estimate; do not introduce randomized restarts or a costly second optimizer.

tried_paradigms.idea: Use scipy.optimize.brute for an exact, bounded neighborhood search over the group-to-node decision
tried_paradigms.description: The current program is a two-level greedy decomposition: it LPT-packs fixed contiguous logical-expert groups onto nodes using raw group load, greedily allocates replicas independently within each resulting node, then LPT-packs replica streams onto GPUs. Its major quality weakness is the first decision: a group is sent to a node before the algorithm knows how much replication will flatten that node's load, so the node assignment can be locally attractive under raw load but poor after replication. Keep the existing algorithm as the deterministic construction of a feasible baseline, identify only the few groups on the highest-load and lowest-load nodes, and encode reassignment of that small set as a discrete vector. Call scipy.optimize.brute once over this bounded Cartesian product, rejecting vectors that violate exactly groups_per_node groups per node. The objective evaluated by brute should be the actual final bottleneck surrogate after running the existing replica allocation and GPU packing for the candidate assignment: lexicographically minimize maximum GPU replica-stream load, then node load range, then sum of squared GPU loads. Apply this only when the selected neighborhood has a safely bounded state count; otherwise retain the current greedy mapping. This is fundamentally different from the previously failed global MILP, min-cost-flow, and one-shot assignment attempts because it searches the nonlinear composed policy that the evaluator actually sees, while retaining fixed-cardinality hierarchy constraints.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Primarily final per-GPU peak load and the inter-node imbalance caused by greedy raw-load group placement; secondarily avoid a runtime regression by restricting exact search to a tiny bottleneck neighborhood.
tried_paradigms.cautions: The adapter shown does not expose the original evaluator's internal score, so the candidate objective must be validated against its actual load metric rather than assumed from the wrapper. Do not brute-force all groups or all layers jointly. Preserve each node's exact group count, physical-experts-per-GPU count, and replica-rank invariants, and use a strict state-count/time cutoff well below the 360-second worker timeout. This is a direct discrete search, not continuous relaxation or hyperparameter tuning.

tried_paradigms.idea: Replace scatter-add updates in LPT packing with direct indexed scatter writes where destinations are unique
tried_paradigms.description: balanced_packing is the dominant repeated kernel: for every group or physical replica position it forms a masked load matrix, chooses one pack per layer, and updates loads and counts. At each position, each row writes to exactly one selected pack, so no two writes collide within that row. Therefore the load update and count update do not require reduction semantics: replace scatter_add_ with scatter_ using the already gathered old value plus the item's weight, and write count plus one directly. This preserves the exact LPT choices, ordering, returned maps, and balancing quality of the current best program, unlike the failed best-exchange proposal that used scatter_add_ as part of a quality-changing local search. The purpose is to reduce reduction-kernel overhead and simplify the update dependency on single-thread CPU execution. Also retain float32 working loads exactly as the current code does, so ties resolve identically unless an intentional deterministic tie rule is added. Since the evaluator isolates execution in one thread and may include algorithm time in its primary score, an exactly quality-preserving kernel reduction can improve the combined score without risking feasibility.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Execution time of both node-level and GPU-level LPT packing while maintaining the current 0.129100 solution quality exactly.
tried_paradigms.cautions: This is valid only because chosen pack indices are unique across rows, not globally unique; use a two-dimensional row/column indexing formulation or per-row scatter_ correctly. Do not replace the argmin tie behavior, do not mutate values before they are read, and benchmark small cases against the old function for bitwise-identical maps and counts. This is not a recommendation to revisit the failed scatter_add_-based exchange heuristic.

tried_paradigms.idea: Use torch.argsort to materialize all marginal replica streams and allocate replicas by global marginal order
tried_paradigms.description: The existing replication loop repeatedly selects argmax(weight[e] / current_count[e]) for every redundant physical slot. This greedy rule is selecting the largest elements from each expert's decreasing marginal stream weight[e]/2, weight[e]/3, and so on, but it pays for one full argmax and indexed update per extra slot. Construct the bounded candidate matrix weight[:, :, None] divided by integer replica counts 2 through num_redundant_experts+1, flatten it per layer, and call torch.argsort once in descending order. Scan only the first num_redundant_experts candidates while accepting an expert's k-th candidate only after its preceding candidates have been accepted; because every stream is monotone decreasing, sorting naturally places predecessors no later than successors except for exact ties, which can be made deterministic with a secondary expert/count key. The accepted candidates define logical replica counts, after which physical replica slots and ranks can be generated in the same canonical order as today. This attacks a different bottleneck from final GPU packing: it preserves the mathematically appropriate discrete replica policy while removing repeated full-vector reductions. It is not the previously failed torch.topk threshold-water-filling proposal: no threshold approximation is used, and the full ordered marginal sequence reproduces the greedy replica-selection rule exactly.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Replica-allocation runtime, particularly workloads with many redundant slots, while retaining the replica counts that minimize the maximum individual replica-stream load under the current per-node constraint.
tried_paradigms.cautions: The flattened candidate tensor has size layers × logical-experts × redundant-slots, so enable this only below a memory threshold; retain the existing incremental argmax loop for large configurations. Stable tie handling matters because a different tie choice can change later GPU packing even if replica counts have equivalent local load. Ensure mandatory first copies are excluded from the candidate list and that generated ranks remain contiguous from zero, since log2phy scatter indexing relies on that invariant.
